clue.text: Woman gets marble put back in wrapping

indicators.note: the clue asks for the turned marble to be placed in the woman, so 'in' signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: a woman can be referred to as she

indicators.note: put back tells us to read the marble word from right to left

parts.note: a taw is a large shooting marble in the children's game

explanation.surface: A woman receives a marble that has been returned to her, wrapped up in cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: A taw is the big shooting marble in the children's game; 'put back' turns it round before 'in' places it within the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A swathe is a band of fabric used for binding or bandaging, so it is a wrapping.

indicators.note: only half the word sketch is complete here, so we keep its first three letters

parts.note: to let on is to reveal or disclose something

explanation.surface: An artist's sketch, only half done, already shows the outline of the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half complete' keeps SKE, the first half of SKETCH; LET ON is an idiom for revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the bare framework or outline of a plan, story or structure.

parts.note: an attaché is a junior diplomat at an embassy; the 's is just a link
d is the usual abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A diplomat's daughter has got married.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attached is spoken for, in a relationship or wedded, so the word fits married.

parts.note: 'he'll' is the contraction of 'he will', that man being he
love means nil in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A greeting that a man is bound to love.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the standard salutation said on meeting someone or answering a phone.

parts.note: a curate is an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest is careful and conscientious.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrupulous work is precise and exact, careful about every detail, hence free of error.

parts.note: to carpet someone is to call them in for a telling-off
a keener is a professional mourner who wails, so a weeper

explanation.surface: Someone scolds an eager housekeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keener' looks like an adjective meaning more eager; here it is the noun, one who keens or wails at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a manual floor-cleaning device with rotating brushes pushed over rugs.

indicators.note: a blunder is a mess-up, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone minimises Nell's rude mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunder' looks like a noun in the surface but acts as the anagram signal on NELLS RUDE, the 'S counting here.
explanation.definitionFit: To undersell is to understate or underrate the merits of something, which is to play it down.

clue.text: A puff atop the discharge pipe is coming

indicators.note: in a down clue, atop means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a puff is a promotional notice, an advertisement or ad
a vent is an outlet through which gas or fluid escapes

explanation.surface: A cloud of smoke rises above the exhaust pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A puff' is an ad, a piece of promotional praise.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival or approach, the coming of someone or something.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of listen are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Pay attention: they are coming to call you up for service.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist someone is to enrol them in the armed forces, as a conscript is drafted.

clue.text: Praise for entry in the next Olympics

indicators.note: an entry in the phrase is a word sitting inside it, spanning next and Olympics

explanation.surface: Applause for an athlete's entry into the next Games.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or glorify, praising highly.

clue.text: Thrill-seeker has lawyer embarrassed by depravity

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
embarrassed people go red in the face
evil is wickedness or depravity

explanation.surface: A risk-taker has a lawyer shamed by corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is a reckless person who seeks out danger for excitement.

clue.text: Stood in London borough creating treachery

parts.note: an actor's stand-in doubled for the star
Ealing is a borough in west London

explanation.surface: Someone substituting in a London borough is creating betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: EALING is a borough of west London, famous for its film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicity in dealings, saying one thing and doing another, amounts to treachery.

indicators.note: keeping means holding other letters within it

parts.note: to ensure is to guarantee
CL is 150 in Roman numerals
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A promise to hold 150 ducks in a farmyard pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound is a fenced or walled area, and an enclosure is just such a fenced-off space.

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
ends are finishes or conclusions

explanation.surface: The queen ends up crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' looks like the noun for crying; it is the verb that rhymes with 'bears', rips.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend is to rip apart, so rends means rips or tears in the verb sense.

clue.text: Works with guerrilla leader and misses visual aid

parts.note: opera is the plural of opus, a work

indicators.note: the leader of guerrilla is its first letter

parts.note: misses are young unmarried women, lasses

explanation.surface: Musical works featuring a rebel commander and missing a visual element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misses' looks like a verb, but it is plural of miss, a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: These small binoculars used at the theatre help the eye see the stage, an aid to vision.

clue.text: A model keeps some servants in accommodation

indicators.note: keeps means holding other letters inside

parts.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car, so T can be a model
part means some of something
men can mean manservants or attendants

explanation.surface: A fashion model employs a few servants at her lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts PARTMEN between A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat or set of rooms is a dwelling, and accommodation means a place to live.

clue.text: Worker to abscond with fast runner

parts.note: a worker ant is the standard crossword worker
to elope is to run off secretly, abscond

explanation.surface: An employee runs away with a speedy athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: This African grazing animal is renowned for its speed, so it is literally a swift runner.

clue.text: Wears tie loosely, so to speak

indicators.note: loosely suggests the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: Wears a tie loosely, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms that flag a figurative expression, meaning in a manner of speaking.

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters are put together poorly, mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone copes poorly with sorrow, which shows up as bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes lingering bitterness or ill will after a dispute, which is resentment.

parts.note: to sponge a surface is to wipe it

explanation.surface: A son scrounges and steals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sponges' suggests freeloading, but here it is cleaning with a sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: To swipe something is informal for stealing it, as one pilfers small items.

indicators.note: to dump something in a place is to drop it there, putting one piece within another
in says where the surplus goes, inside the river

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
the rest is what remains, the surplus

explanation.surface: Hurriedly throw any excess into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is a musical tempo marking meaning very fast, so quickly.

clue.text: Argument about the way that's least desirable

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for argument is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or argument
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A dispute about the route which is the least appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of bad describes the most undesirable thing, the least desirable.

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to present something is to show it

explanation.surface: Right now it is time for a tango performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at this moment, currently, which is what now means.

clue.text: Art supporter finds peace on lake

parts.note: ease is peace of mind, freedom from worry
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A patron of the arts finds tranquillity by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art supporter' suggests a patron; it is the stand that literally supports a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame that holds a painter's canvas upright, physically supporting artwork.

indicators.note: about means around, so the advert wraps round the port

parts.note: a poster is a printed advertisement
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

explanation.surface: An advertisement for port wine is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink; it is Rio, the port city, which 'about' puts inside POSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Posterior is a jocular word for the buttocks, which is one sense of bottom.

indicators.note: about means around, so the angry word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: sore can mean angry or annoyed, especially in American usage
W is the cricket scoreboard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricketer cursed, cross about losing a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declared' suggests a cricket declaration, but it means stated on oath.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to state solemnly or under oath, so swore means declared.

parts.note: short means brief
an age is a period of time, an era

explanation.surface: A brief time of hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: A famine is an extreme scarcity, especially of food, so it is a lack or dearth.

clue.text: Claim supporter tucked into the booze

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside something

parts.note: ale is beer, booze
a leg supports a table or a body

explanation.surface: A fan is getting stuck into the drink, so someone asserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating or drinking heartily, but here it only places one piece within the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, which is to claim it.
